evals.prompt: Audit our Python codebase for cyclomatic/cognitive complexity hotspots and maintainability regressions, then refactor a 95-line `calculate_shipping_fee` function (`radon` grade D, CC = 24) that nests 6 levels of `if/elif` country, tier, weight, and promo-code checks with magic float literals.
evals.expected_output: Measures baseline complexity with `radon cc . -n C`, `lizard -C 15 .`, `radon mi . -n B`, and `wily build .` / `wily diff`, then flattens `calculate_shipping_fee` below CC < 11 using early guard clauses, a configuration class (`FeeConfig`) and lookup table (`dict`) replacing magic numbers and `if/elif` chains, and extracted focused helper functions, re-measuring afterward.
expectations: Runs `radon cc . -n C` (targeting CC < 11), `lizard -C 15 .` (targeting cognitive <= 15), and `radon mi . -n B` (targeting MI >= 65) to quantify complexity before and after refactoring
Flattens deep `if/elif/else` nesting using early-return guard clauses
Extracts scattered magic numbers into a named configuration class and replaces `if/elif` rate branches with a dictionary lookup table
Breaks distinct responsibilities into focused sub-functions and verifies complexity metrics improved while all tests pass

evals.prompt: A 780-line `src/orders/manager.py` file mixes order models, pricing rules, webhook formatting, and 14 repetitive `if config.email.field: config.email.field = substitute_secret(...)` blocks, plus repeats `Literal['use', 'only', 'refresh'] | None` 8 times.
evals.expected_output: Splits the >500-line code file into focused modules (`< 500` lines each), replaces the 14 repetitive field `if`-statements with a `getattr`/`setattr` loop over field names, extracts the repeated `Literal[...]` union into a shared `TypeAlias` (module-level or `types.py`), and verifies improvements with `radon`, `lizard`, `wily diff`, and `pytest`.
expectations: Identifies the >500-line file and splits it into cohesive modules under 500 lines
Replaces the repetitive field-checking `if`-statements with a `getattr`/`setattr` loop over an explicit list of field names
Extracts the repeated `Literal[...]` union into a single named `TypeAlias` (at module level or in `types.py`)
Tracks complexity reduction with `wily diff` and runs tests to confirm coverage and behavior are preserved

evals.prompt: Set up complexity thresholds and historical trend tracking for our Python project in CI/CD so pull requests cannot introduce functions with cyclomatic complexity >= C (11+), cognitive complexity > 15, or maintainability index < 65.
evals.expected_output: Adds `radon`, `lizard`, `xenon`, and `wily` to `[dependency-groups]` `dev`, configures CI/CD threshold gates using `xenon` (alongside `radon cc . -n C`, `radon mi . -n B`, and `lizard -C 15 .`), initializes `wily build .` with `wily diff` for tracking trends across git history, and notes `py-git-hooks` / `py-quality-setup` for pre-commit and tool setup.
expectations: Declares `radon`, `lizard`, `xenon`, and `wily` in `[dependency-groups]` `dev` as the complexity toolchain
Uses `xenon` alongside `radon cc . -n C`, `radon mi . -n B`, and `lizard -C 15 .` to enforce cyclomatic (< 11), maintainability (>= 65), and cognitive (<= 15) thresholds in CI/CD
Uses `wily build .` and `wily diff` (e.g., `wily diff HEAD~10`) to track complexity and maintainability trends across git history
Checks code file line counts (splitting files > 500 lines unless unavoidable) and verifies all tests pass
